A v123 .state file holds the initial state, 7 bytes, the current state (its first header field is a 32-bit hash, not the version), 2 bytes, then the action list. Player records follow polytopiamapmodelgo's post-v114 layout plus 1 trailing byte (equal to the tribe id). All 27 saves decode to the last byte. Actions store what was done (move, attack origin and target, train, research), not the results, so combat damage has to be checked by replaying actions in a simulator and comparing with the saved current state.
rules.evidence: verify/state_v123.py read_state(), 27 of 27 saves, 0 unparsed bytes. Action payload sizes are confirmed for v123 only for type 20 (StartMatch, 10 bytes). | Played save 9847d452 (turn 6, 130 actions) parses to the last byte. Action layouts follow polytopiamapmodelgo; StartMatch (type 20) is 1 byte, and the file ends with a 9-byte trailer (3 zero bytes, the state hash, the action count). Confirmed in v123: Build, Train, Move, Capture, Research, CityReward, ExamineRuins, EndTurn, StartMatch. Not yet seen: Attack, Promote, Upgrade, CityLevelUp and others. | Bot-war save 6e1bf8e0 (Massive, 16 players; exports at turns 5, 11, 15; 2,157 actions with 300 attacks) parses exactly. Sizes now confirmed by an exact end: Attack 21, Recover 9, Promote 9, Upgrade 11, CityLevelUp 9, types 18/24 9, 27/30 10, 28 3, and a new type 38 (9 bytes: player + tile, from Cymanti). Player tasks: type 9 carries 6 bytes, like 1 and 5.

rules.rule: Wiki Ruin page: uniform pick among the rewards eligible at that ruin. 10 stars (always); a random free tech from the currently researchable ones (tree not finished); +3 population to the capital (must own one; otherwise the highest-level capital); a free Explorer (5x5 fog condition, not on mountains, Cymanti not on water); a Veteran Swordsman (land only; was a Giant before 2.0.58); a Veteran Rammer carrying a Warrior (water only); Lost City (Aquarion on deep ocean: a level-3 walled city with 4 shallow tiles). The unit must start its turn on the ruin, and examining uses its turn.
rules.level: L1 (wiki + PolyEnv's uniform pool agree; the weights are untested)
rules.evidence: polytopia.fandom.com/wiki/Ruin fetched 2026-10-23. Open point: the wiki fetch read the Explorer condition as 'no tile in the 5x5 explored' while PolyEnv says 'some tile still hidden'. A ruin log decides it.

rules.rule: Damage = round_half_up(aF/(aF+dF) x atk x 4.5), with aF = atk x hp/maxhp and dF = def x hp/maxhp x bonus. A melee attacker that kills moves into the tile.
rules.evidence: Engine replay of bot-war save 6e1bf8e0 (468 attacks to turn 15) vs checkpoints at turns 5/11/15. Exact-HP matches with the rule, then without: banker's rounding loses 0/5/4 matches; no move-in loses 3/0/5.

rules.rule: The counter-attack uses the defender's bonus-boosted defence force: ret = round(dF/(aF+dF) x def x 4.5). The wiki and calculator are right; PolyEnv is wrong.
rules.evidence: Engine replay of bot-war save 6e1bf8e0 (468 attacks to turn 15) vs checkpoints at turns 5/11/15. Exact-HP matches with the rule, then without: 63/77/93 with the bonus vs 60/70/87 without.

rules.rule: Defence bonus 1.5 in your own city for Fortify units only (4 with walls); 1.5 on forest with Archery and on mountain with Climbing (the tech is required); otherwise 1.
rules.evidence: Engine replay of bot-war save 6e1bf8e0 (468 attacks to turn 15) vs checkpoints at turns 5/11/15. Exact-HP matches with the rule, then without: no city bonus 58/66/83; city bonus for any unit 63/75/89; terrain bonus without tech 60/74/86.

rules.rule: The defender hits back only if the attacker is within the defender's range.
rules.evidence: Engine replay of bot-war save 6e1bf8e0 (468 attacks to turn 15) vs checkpoints at turns 5/11/15. Exact-HP matches with the rule, then without: retaliating at any range: 63/73/89.

rules.rule: Action meanings inferred from context: 27 = a free, repeatable diplomacy action aimed at a foreign capital (player, capital x,y, owner id), NOT Establish Embassy (charging an embassy price breaks 14 exact player-turns; the same pair repeats on several turns): it is OFFER PEACE (see DIPLO-PEACE); 30 = embassy/peace follow-up on the same capital; 28 = diplomacy reply at turn start (player, other player, flag); 38 = Shaman Swarm: adjacent friendly units get extra movement (Swift, UnitEffect 6), no attack bonus (Jason in game 2026-10-23, the save's Swift effect, and Polyfish's v115 note agree; the old +0.5 attack reading changes nothing in any replay and is off); 24 = Explode (Cymanti Boomchi); Build type 30 = Enchant Animal (Elyrion, spawns a Polytaur). Type 18 = BREAK ICE (see ACTION-18-BREAK-ICE): payload player + the acting unit's tile. Profile over 79 uses in 33 games: bots only (never the human player), only in the three 16-player games; payload = player + tile; the tile always holds the actor's own unit (Warrior 60, Rider 6, others); 59/79 right after that unit moved; enemy unit within 2 tiles in 70/79; no change to the unit (HP, position, effects, flags) or the tile; the unit takes no further action that turn. 14 = Examine Ruins.

rules.rule: A Giant that goes to sea becomes a Juggernaut (not a Raft); on landing it is a Giant again.

rules.rule: A land unit that kills a unit standing on its OWN tribe's port moves in and boards (it becomes a boat); on an enemy port it stays where it was.
rules.evidence: Own port: boarded 4/4 (e15f392c t12 unit 196, t14 unit 145; af181c8f t14 unit 271, t19 unit 402). Enemy port: stayed 2/2 (e15f392c t13 unit 60; af181c8f t21 unit 401). Without the own-port condition the bot war turn 11 dropped 90 -> 89. Engine RULES port_kill_embark.

rules.rule: A forced spawn can push a land unit onto a neighbouring port of its own tribe, where it boards (own-port condition assumed from PORT-KILL-EMBARK).
rules.evidence: af181c8f turns 15 and 21: an Ai-Mo Warrior trained in the city at (20,22), pushed out by the Giant reward, ends up as the passenger of a boat on the port at (19,21) (direction toward the map centre, as in Polyfish). Engine RULES push_onto_port; net +1 exact in the per-turn replay.

rules.evidence: af181c8f: Xin-xi Scoutship 501 at (20,9) on turn 22 and Rammership 499 at (21,13) on turn 25, both carrying a Swordsman on flood value 4. Engine RULES algae_keeps_boats.

rules.rule: When a tribe loses its last city, its remaining units are removed.
rules.evidence: af181c8f: Kickoo lost its last city on turn 10 (DestroyedTurn 10, by Xin-xi); its leftover Warriors are gone by the turn-12 save. Engine RULES no_cities_no_units.

rules.rule: Tile effects live in the save as FloodedFlag + FloodedValue = the TileEffect enum (1 Flooded, 4 Algae). Aquarion-flooded fields and forests: a boat that sails onto one stays a boat, and a land unit walks on it without boarding; a flooded city counts as plain land. Cymanti algae on water: land units walk on it like land. Seen: 242 flooded land tiles near Aquarion, 24 algae tiles in Cymanti land.
rules.evidence: all saves (unit kind by terrain and flag); engine RULES flood_keeps_form, algae_is_land

rules.rule: A boat's save record always has promotion 0; the passenger record keeps the veteran level. The boat's Health is live; the passenger copy is a stale snapshot from boarding.
rules.level: L3 (all boats with passengers across the saves)
rules.evidence: engine state.py

rules.rule: After a melee kill: a boat moving onto land drops its passenger (who gets their id back); a land unit does not follow a kill into water; a water-only unit (Shark, Raychi, Puffer, Jelly, Crab: seen only on water, flooded tiles or in cities) does not follow a kill onto dry land.
rules.evidence: e15f392c turns 9 and 15; bot war turn 11 +2, turn 15 +1; engine RULES kill_move_lands, water_units_stay

rules.rule: Splash (Bomber, Fire Dragon): every enemy next to the target takes half the damage a direct attack would deal it, floored, with no retaliation. Same formula as Explode.
rules.evidence: e15f392c turn 13 (Bomber hit a Rider next to its target); bot war turn 11 88 -> 90; engine RULES attack_splash

rules.rule: Poison (v115+): a poisoned unit's defence is halved, bonus included (Polyfish; the old wiki said -30% and no bonus). Sources: poison-skill attackers poison their target (a poison defender poisons a contact attacker); Cymanti Fungi poisons non-Cymanti units of other owners standing on it at each end of turn; Clathrus poisons enemies stepping on it. Cure: Recover removes poison instead of healing (wiki; not yet seen in a save).
rules.level: L3 for the -50% (e15f392c turn 11: a Raychi one-shots a 10 HP Warrior that ended a turn on Fungi; 10 damage exactly), L1 for the cure

rules.rule: No retaliation when the defender's tribe cannot see the attacker: an Archer or Catapult shot from a tile it can't see does not shoot back. Seeing = the tile is explored (explored tiles show enemies live), or within current vision (radius 1; 2 for Scout units or units on mountains).

rules.rule: Forced-spawn pushes follow Polyfish's rule (functions.rs calculate_pushable_position) with two measured refinements: (1) the last-move direction is the unit's last move ever, not only this turn (af181c8f t4: a Warrior that walked north the turn before was pushed north, not toward the centre); (2) a multi-tile move's direction rounds to the nearest of the 8 directions, ties toward the axis ((-2,-1) pushes on (-1,0): 6e1bf8e0 t11, e15f392c t13). An enemy of the acting player is pushed the opposite way; a unit that never moved goes toward the map centre. A blocked or unsuitable tile is skipped for the next direction either side, nearer the centre first. Open: a Warrior trained in its city and never moved was pushed AWAY from the centre (af181c8f t10).

A 7/10 Boomchi exploding next to a poisoned 6/10 Warrior and a poisoned 5/15 Defender took the Warrior to 1 and killed the Defender; without the halving the engine left them at 2 and 1.
rules.level: L3 (2/2 targets in one explosion land on the saved HP; replay A/B 13 -> 12 unit misses, stars hold)
rules.evidence: engine RULES explode_poison_halves; af181c8f t15 (Boomchi id313 at 25,15; save t15 UnitEffects [1] on both targets)

rules.rule: A pushed land unit boards onto its own port only when the port is its first-choice push direction; as a fallback the port is skipped like other water.
rules.evidence: Engine pushes onto an own port: 6e1bf8e0 t6 (Defender, first choice), af181c8f t9 x2 and t10 (first choice) all land on the port in the saves; 6e1bf8e0 t11 action 1372, Zebasi Warrior 257 in (21,5): first choice (20,6) blocked, fallbacks port (21,6) and (20,5); it was on (20,5) (moves from there at 1548). Engine RULES push_port_first_only; miss.py units 4725/4733 -> 4725/4732.

rules.rule: A water ruin's unit reward is a boat with a passenger; the veteran level is on the passenger record (the boat record shows 0), so a Rammership with a veteran Warrior has 15 HP.
rules.evidence: 6e1bf8e0 t14 action 2035: Bardur examined ruin (18,21) (ocean); t15 save: Rammership 431 (15 HP, created 14) carrying Warrior 432 at promotion 1. Engine RULES ruin_boat_passenger; miss.py units 4725/4732 -> 4726/4732.

rules.rule: Each tile's UnitDirection (5 bytes after UnitEffects) holds the unit's facing in byte 2: 0 NW, 1 W, 2 SW, 3 S, 4 SE, 5 E, 6 NE, 7 N. It follows the unit's last move (rounded to 8 directions); this is the hidden direction the forced-spawn push uses, so pushes read it from the save instead of guessing. Units that never moved also carry a facing, but it doesn't predict their push (af181c8f t10), so they keep the toward-attacker / toward-centre fallback.
rules.level: L3 (save field matches the last logged move's direction for about 85% of units with a move, 2 games; replay A/B 6 -> 5 unit misses, stars hold)
rules.evidence: engine RULES push_saved_facing; verify/state_v123.py UnitDirection; af181c8f t15 (ruin push of Raychi id94 lands east as its facing says)

rules.rule: Breaking a peace disbands the breaker's units inside the ex-ally's borders, with no refund; the breaker cannot attack that turn. Peace forbids attacks both ways and lets units pass through each other's territory and use their roads. Bots accept peace only at a 'Great' opinion.
rules.level: L3 for the disband (Jason in game, 2026-10-23); L0 for the rest (cannot attack that turn, units frozen)
rules.evidence: Jason's pasted summary, 2026-10-23, undated source. The one broken peace in the saves had no units inside the other's borders, so nothing to test yet. Not in the engine. | 2026-10-23: now in the engine as RULES peace_break_disbands (on, best guess; labelled unverified in data/rule_levels.json). On or off changes no replay score (no disband happens in any save). Polyfish v115 BreakPeaceMove only resets the relation (no disband) and notes that breaking should end the breaker's turn: a second source on the turn end, none on the disband. | Wiki (fandom, search snippet, undated): the breaker cannot attack that tribe that turn, all the breaker's active units are frozen for the rest of the turn, and its units inside the other tribe's borders are disbanded with no refund. Likely the same text Jason pasted, so not an independent source: stays L0. The 'units frozen' part is not in the engine. | Jason, 2026-10-23: when he broke a peace treaty in game, his units inside the ex-ally's territory were disbanded. Not in any save yet; the engine switch peace_break_disbands stays on and is no longer flagged unverified.

rules.rule: Break Ice (action 18) uses the unit's action, so only a Dash unit can move and then break ice in the same turn.
rules.level: L3 (130/130 move-then-break uses in the saves are Dash units; Jason in game)
rules.evidence: Jason's in-game text 2026-10-23 (see ACTION-18-BREAK-ICE). Saves, all per-turn intervals (engine/replay.py LOG, 2026-10-23): 130 break-ice actions came right after the same unit moved that turn; 128 were Dash units (v123 cards, else data/units.json: Warrior, Rider, Raychi, Tridention, Rammer...), 2 were a Raft, which has no Dash on any source. The Raft may borrow its passenger's Dash, or breaking ice may not need Dash: test item. Engine: RULES break_ice_after_move_needs_dash only counts violations (legality check for the forward model), no state change. | Wiki (fandom Unit page, search snippet, undated): Break Ice is available to all units except those with Freeze Area (Mooni, Gaami) and needs at least one adjacent ice tile; it says nothing about Dash. That fits the 2 Raft cases better than 'Dash only': conflict, test item. | Re-test 2026-10-23 after Jason's note (upgrading a Raft to a Scoutship gives it Dash and 2-tile vision, which is how those boats broke ice after moving): with a per-turn 'moved this turn' mark (last_from now persists across turns for push direction, which had made a turn-11 move look like a turn-12 one) and the upstream boat fixes, all 130 move-then-break uses are Dash units, 0 exceptions. The earlier 2 'Raft' cases were engine bookkeeping, not a rule break.

rules.rule: An idle unit (no move, no attack that turn) heals at its owner's End Turn as if it had Recovered: +4 in friendly territory, +2 in neutral or enemy territory, never past max HP. Poisoned units don't heal. In the replay only the human player's (AutoPlay 0) idle units heal; AI idle units don't in any save.
rules.level: L3 (Jason in game, 23 Oct 2026 + 1 save case af181c8f t15; applying it to AI players adds 57 replay misses, so the engine keeps it human-only)
rules.evidence: engine RULES idle_auto_recover; Jason's in-game answer 23 Oct 2026; af181c8f t15 (Rider id260 6 -> 10)

rules.rule: When a push's first-choice tile is blocked, the game tries one step counter-clockwise, then one step clockwise, then two steps each way, alternating outward. If no tile is open, the pushed unit is removed. In the engine's grid order (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW, y pointing down), the game's counter-clockwise side is the next entry in that list: the screen view is mirrored relative to the grid. Polyfish's nearer-the-centre tie-break is wrong.
rules.level: L3 (Jason in game, 23 Oct 2026 + the one deciding save push, af181c8f t10; no save has a push with no open tile)
rules.evidence: engine RULES push_ccw_first, push_no_room_removes; Jason's in-game answer 23 Oct 2026; af181c8f t10 (south blocked, Warrior id169 went SW, not SE)

rules.rule: Push direction for a unit with no move: (a) if it was attacked, toward the attacker; (b) otherwise the way a new unit faces: toward the map centre (W//2, H//2), nearest of the 8 directions by angle. Blocked: counter-clockwise side first (PUSH-DIRECTION).
rules.evidence: Saves: units on their spawn tile that never moved face the centre by nearest angle in 824/871 cases (sign only 543, axis-rounding 756). 6e1bf8e0 t9 action 1062: trainee at (2,9) faces (1,1), (3,10) blocked, CCW next (2,10) = save; t13 1849: Swordsman 317 hit from (17,1) pushed onto (17,1); t14 Giant 387 (16,2)->(16,3). Engine RULES push_toward_attacker, push_centre_round='angle'; miss.py units 4727/4729 -> 4727/4728.

rules.rule: Ruin reward frequencies measured from the saves (data/distributions.json, tools/distributions.py): stars 14, population 16, tech 11, unit 7, explorer 6 of 54 classified ruins (2 unresolved). Consistent with a uniform pick over the eligible rewards (RUIN-REWARD): chi-square vs 1/5 each = 6.95, df 4, p = 0.14. Water ruins (n=10): no explorer seen (0/10). The simulator should sample uniformly over the eligible pool; the measured shares are the check.
rules.level: L3 (measured, n=54 resolved of 56; explorer/pop read from soft signals)
rules.evidence: Per-turn saves 09a5bf1e, 1bf60251, 6e1bf8e0, af181c8f, e15f392c. Each examined ruin classified from the saves either side: unit = unit created that turn on the ruin tile; tech = tech gained without Research; stars = star check +10; explorer = 30+ newly visible tiles the replayed units don't explain (false-positive rate 1/674 player-turns; city Explorer rewards reach it 31/35); pop = capital TotalPopulation +3 beyond builds (false-positive 8/709). Cross-check: whole-game free techs per ruin 14/57 = 0.25 (95% 0.15-0.37). Polyfish (sim/pfcore) has the reward enum but no weights; PolyEnv and the wiki say uniform.

rules.rule: Aquarion amphibious units (Mermaid 46, Swordsmaid 48) stand on shallow water with no water tech (only the start tech 45): no Fishing-slot tech needed. Ocean: seen only for players holding Navigation and Marine Life (46), so the ocean rule is still open.

On Ocean: 3 records (2 Mermaids, 1 Shark), all owners with Navigation and 46. Polyfish v115 lets Amphibious units onto water only with a tech that opens water (none for Aquarion), which made 142 logged Aquarion moves illegal (pf-loader).

rules.rule: Bot first research, decision list on start techs and the 3x3 around the capital (initialTiles): Aquarion -> its tribe tech (id 47); Polaris -> IceFishing or Sledding; a tribe whose start tech opens Mining (Climbing or Smithery: XinXi, Vengir) -> Mining if 2+ metal, or 1+ metal and no water; else any water tile -> Fishing (if not known); else 2+ fruit -> Organization; else 2+ game -> Hunting; else metal -> Climbing; else Riding. Misses are mostly Kickoo (starts with Fishing; next tech varies) and Oumaji (FreeSpirit 2/2).
rules.level: L3 (measured, statistical: 62/77 training = 81% vs 55% always-Fishing; held-out ed6cb932 14/15 vs 10/15)
rules.evidence: tools/bot_rules.py -> data/bot_rules.json; 77 bot players in 6 training games, 15 in held-out ed6cb932 (scored once after the rule was fixed on training misses).

rules.rule: A bot unit that has a visible hostile target within range at the moment of its first action attacks (in place or after a move) unless it stands in its own city or is a Defender. Attack rates: field unit with a predicted kill 217/302 (72%), field no kill 294/541 (54%), own city with kill 31/110, own city no kill 17/92, Defender no kill 14/131 (11%). Unit HP, relation (who hit whom), human vs bot target barely matter. Not deterministic: treat as these probabilities.
rules.level: L3 (measured, statistical: 791/1195 = 66% vs 51% majority; held-out 10/10, too small to judge)
rules.evidence: tools/bot_attacks.py (replay + engine fight() on the live state just before each bot unit's first action) -> data/bot_attacks.csv; tools/bot_rules.py scores it. 1195 decisions in 5 games with bot attacks; Raft/Mooni/Boomchi excluded.

rules.rule: With 2+ targets in range at the attack, a bot hits: a predicted kill first, then the target with the least return damage, then the most expensive unit type. 65% for attacks without a prior move (n=157, random 42%), 58% after a move (n=367, random 44%; the bot probably chose the target before moving, from squares we do not enumerate). Max damage, lowest HP, unit id, nearest, relation all score 50-57%.
rules.level: L3 (measured, statistical: 313/524 = 60% vs 44% random; held-out 2/3, too small)
rules.evidence: tools/bot_attacks.py + tools/bot_rules.py; engine fight() predictions; 19 of 1210 attacks hit a target not on our list (fog/peace/range model).

rules.rule: v123 Cymanti research the base Fishing, Sailing, Ramming, Navigation and Diplomacy (no Hydrology, Synergy or Oceantology in their place). They train the Raychi with Sailing, the Boomchi with Ramming, and build Algae with Fishing. Moth with Diplomacy (n=1).
rules.evidence: All saves (2026-10-24, pf-port): Cymanti player records hold Fishing 44, Sailing 35, Navigation 30, Ramming 23, Diplomacy 2 of 57; never Hydrology (37), Synergy or Recycling; Oceantology (49) once, next to Navigation. Every Raychi training (21/21) comes with Sailing, every Boomchi training (35/35) with Ramming, every Algae build (12/12) with Fishing; the one Moth training with Diplomacy. Polyfish v115 had Hydrology replace Sailing (unlocking Raychi, Boomchi, Algae), Synergy replace Diplomacy (Moth), Oceantology replace Navigation.

rules.rule: Cymanti algae (flood value 4) doesn't stop the movement of Cymanti units or of boats; they move on through it. Other tribes' land units on algae untested (Polyfish v115 stops every unit without Creep/Fly there).
